prize_parts.citation: For a visionary, densely patterned Romanian prose, grounded in a poet's language, that builds memory, the body, dream and metaphysical speculation into large-scale imaginative architectures across a whole body of work.

statement.case_for: I keep B014 as my single preferred configuration after the exchange. The reasons are literary. First, voice: the supplied description and public knowledge of Blinding and Solenoid point to a voice recognisable as his alone. Second, form: memory, the body, dream and cosmology are held in one patterned syntax, so the sentence and the large structure carry the ambition, not the subject matter. Third, sustained quality: poetry underlies the prose and the major novels extend one another, which supports a whole-oeuvre citation instead of a one-title citation. Round 1 gave no concrete evidence that the later work only repeats the earlier motifs. The reservations are real, but they are risks that no colleague has substantiated. I have not counted the identical first-place preferences as merit, and the six round-1 files record shared caveats, not independent verification. I also tightened the citation wording in response to the chair's question. It now says prose grounded in a poet's language and does not name poetry as a co-equal achievement, because the poetic strand is the least visible part of the evidence in translation. Attribution is unambiguous: one writer, one prize part, one credited name.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is unchanged and unresolved. The effect depends on Romanian sentence rhythm and density that I can judge only through translations of uneven quality, and I have not read the originals or independently verified any source. The poetry and early work are thinner in my evidence than the major novels, so the whole-oeuvre claim is partly an extrapolation from the best-known books. Length and elaboration may shade into repetition in some volumes. If the committee's reading showed that the late work repeats earlier motifs without new formal solutions, or that the density does not survive outside the best-known novels, the claim for the whole oeuvre would weaken considerably and I would revisit this configuration. A further risk is that I am preferring an inward, metaphysical project because it is easy to state in a citation, when a less summarisable but equally strong oeuvre may be underweighted.

responses.point: Sem-Sandberg treats the sentence as the unit of Cărtărescu's ambition and reads the poetry as the origin of the prose. He cites the patterned structure of the trilogy and Solenoid as the strongest evidence he can offer, and asks me which specific Adonis poems or sequences a non-Arabic reader could trust.
responses.response: I accept his framing, and it is why I changed my citation wording. The structural evidence for a poetic origin is stronger than any direct evidence I hold about the poetry, so I now say prose grounded in a poet's language. Poetry and prose are no longer named as equal pillars. On Adonis, I cannot meet his challenge. Beyond the two representative works in the supplied entry, I cannot point to particular poems or sequences that carry the claimed prosodic renewal in a way a non-Arabic reader could check. I rely on secondary accounts, as he suspected. That is a reason to lower my confidence in Adonis, and I act on it below. It is not a literary reservation about the poetry. I also agree with him that the sentence-level claim for Cărtărescu is only partly checkable, and I apply that to my own case.

responses.point: Mattson names repetition as the main risk, since length and elaboration may become repetition in some volumes. She keeps Cărtărescu first because of the poetry-to-prose arc, and asks in her Michon response whether a small, refined oeuvre meets the standard of a prize for a whole body of work.
responses.response: The repetition risk is the one I would most want tested, and it can be tested only by readers of the translated novels and poetry saying which volumes they find weakest. From public knowledge I can name only Blinding and Solenoid as the best-known peaks, and I cannot rank the volumes between them without claiming a reading I do not have. On Michon, I keep my seventh-place view for the reason she describes. The compression is a real achievement, but the case rests almost entirely on style, and I cannot show range and development from a small corpus. I do not think size alone disqualifies him. I would revisit him if someone could show, from the works, how the later books differ in kind from Small Lives.

responses.point: Swärd's response says I noted that Carson's later work may be less consistent. She also says Can Xue stays an alternative because her strangeness may partly be a translation effect, and she rejects a very low ranking for Can Xue because sustained radicalism is not only a translation artefact.
responses.response: A correction first, which the chair also flagged: my round-1 file made no statement about Carson's later work being uneven, so that attribution should not enter the record. I ranked Carson third on the strength of her formal invention and hold no verified view of her bibliography. On Can Xue I agree with her that radical formal consistency over decades is not a translation artefact alone, and the point shifts my alternatives (see below). I keep her below Cărtărescu for Swärd's own reason, that the unity of a deliberately uniform method is harder to state in a whole-oeuvre citation than the cumulative architecture of the Romanian cycles. I read that as an open question about development, not a verdict against her.

responses.point: Olsson says his Adonis case depends on prosody and diction that translation loses, so he treats Adonis as the principal alternative with lower confidence. He also concedes that his eighth-place ranking of Can Xue understated her case, though he still wants evidence of development across her work. In his conflict note he asks the committee to test whether he overvalues a metaphysical, inward project.
responses.response: His candour about Adonis is persuasive, and it applies to my own second-place ranking in the same way. We both rely on reputation and secondary accounts for a claim that lies in the Arabic. His concession on Can Xue is the right reading: her translated prose can at least be tested by non-Arabic readers for repetition or deepening, which I cannot say of Adonis's prosody. I therefore reverse the order of my alternatives. Can Xue becomes the first and Adonis the second. This reflects what the committee can verify, not any change in my view of Adonis's significance. I also take his invitation to test the metaphysical bias seriously. It is a risk I share, and I flag it in my case against so that it can be tested.

responses.point: Palm leans toward reading recurrence in the Cărtărescu cycles as an architectural principle, while calling that a judgment, not a verified fact. She also says the committee should test the whole-oeuvre claim against the poetry and earlier work, not rely on the trilogy and Solenoid alone.
responses.response: I agree with both parts. The distinction between recurrence as architecture and recurrence as accumulation is the central unresolved question, and it cannot be answered from summaries. I lean toward architecture, as she does, but I call that a judgment and I would not put it in a citation as fact. Her call to test the earlier work and poetry is the right test of the whole-oeuvre claim. Since the committee's evidence on those strands is thin, I have worded the citation to rest on the prose grounded in a poet's language, which is the part I can best defend.

uncertainties: Whether the metaphysical density and formal control of Cărtărescu's work are sustained across the whole corpus, including the poetry and early work, or lie mainly in the best-known novels. The late work could extend or only repeat earlier motifs, and public summaries cannot settle this.
How far the Romanian sentence rhythm survives translation, and how uneven the translations are across the large novels. I have not read the originals or independently verified any source.
Whether Can Xue's deliberately uniform method deepens across decades or recurs, and what share of her large Chinese-language output is available in translation.

Adonis's prosodic and intertextual achievement in Arabic cannot be verified by me through translation. It also remains open how far his essays and public commentary should enter a citation, which I would confine to the poetry.
Whether the citation should name poetry and prose together or prose grounded in a poet's language, given that the poetic strand is the least visible part of the translated evidence.
Whether a co-opted member's vote counts in committee is not documented in the supplied profile, so my simulated vote is a modeling assumption.
statement.conflict_note: No candidate-related conflict is apparent from the supplied profile, which records no connection to any shortlisted writer. I am co-opted as Permanent Secretary and my own work is literary non-fiction. That is context and not evidence of preference for any candidate. My Nobel biography drew on Nobel Foundation and family archives, which is not a link to any shortlisted writer. In this round I also note that the attribution to me of a Carson-consistency concern does not appear in my own round-1 file, and I disclose this without adjudicating it.
